text: hey I appreciate the comment but this is not accurate the understanding of Elohim is a reference to judges is a post-biblical Innovation Elohim was
never used as a reference to judges in the Hebrew Bible it was always a reference to Gods now sometimes it was a
sarcastic reference to entities that only other peoples thought were Gods but it never meant judges that arose within
rabbinic debates about the meaning of certain passages and specifically Genesis 6 which had been reinterpreted
as a reference to angels in the Greco-Roman period but in the rabbinic period there were debates that this couldn't be Angels either because there was no sexual compatibility between
angels and Humanity or because Angels could not be disobedient to God and so a reading of Bene Elohim in Genesis 6 as a
reference to humans arose as an alternative but we can even see the author of John having Jesus interprets
Psalm 82 as a reference to Gods now Jesus is interpreting this according to a later rabbinic reading that
understands the gods of Psalm 82 to be the Israelites at Sinai who become immortal upon their initial reception of
the law which frees them from the power of the Angel of Death rendering them Immortal rendering them Gods but then
upon sinning with the golden calf they are then condemned to mortality as it says in Psalm 82 and so they return to
being humans and that's John 10's reading which we see in some later rabbinic literature but even that is an innovation on what the psalm originally
referred to now the reading I'm about to share is based on a paper I published in 2018 in the Journal of biblical literature on Psalm 82 as a Psalm of

and if you'd like a more thorough breakdown of what the word Elohim meant in the Hebrew Bible and how gods were understood anciently that is the topic
of the first half of my book adonai's Divine Images This Is An Open Access publication it is also freely available on my link tree so originally composed
in the late exilic or the post-exilic period Psalm 82 is a condemnation of the patron deities of the other nations who
were negligent in their duties to Social and to Cosmic Justice in allowing the exile to take place and so Adonai the
god of Israel whose people are outside of adonai's inheritance and therefore cannot access their deity Adonai
condemns them to mortality which basically deposes them from their seats on the Divine Council leaving those
seats empty for Adonai to take over in order to extend their inheritance their purview their sovereignty over all the
Earth so that the exiled Judah Heights can access their deity outside the land of Israel outside adonai's inheritance
and this is what the psalmist calls on Adonai to do in the very last verse rise up o God Kuma Elohim and judge the Earth for you will inherit All Nations
basically adonai's inheritance which we see given in Deuteronomy 32 8 and 9 has now been expanded Beyond just the land
of Israel to cover all nations so that all the people of the Judean Jewish diaspora in whatever Nation they find
themselves can access and can worship Adonai who previously had been limited to the land of Israel so Psalm 82 is a
rhetorical universalization of Adonai it is a way to expand adonai's purview and sovereignty to cover all nations so that
worshipers of Adonai can worship their deity can access the deities power and agency in any Nation on the earth so
throughout the Hebrew Bible Elohim always means Gods sometimes it is sarcastic frequently it is not it is used in reference to people and to
